answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by locking a refundable saffron bond per identity that unlocks only after three epochs of continuous activity. Each bond also requires solving a quartz-timed proof whose difficulty scales with recent joins sharing the same hardware fingerprint, generating a ripple of higher marginal compute costs. An attacker creating N clones must fund N locked bonds and pay N escalating puzzle solves; detection of correlated errors jointly slashes the whole cluster, so total cost grows faster than linear in headcount.
